back_translation: Thus says the Lord GOD: The gate of the inner court that faces east must remain shut during the six working days, but on the Sabbath day and on the day of the New Moon it shall be opened.

The prince shall enter from outside through the portico of the gate and stand by the gatepost, while the priests offer his burnt offering and peace offerings; he shall bow in worship at the threshold of the gate and then go out, but the gate shall not be shut until evening.
The people of the land shall also bow in worship before the LORD at the entrance of that gate on the Sabbaths and New Moons.
The burnt offering that the prince offers to the LORD on the Sabbath day shall be six unblemished male lambs and an unblemished ram.
The grain offering for the ram shall be one ephah, and the grain offering for the lambs as much as he is able to give, with a hin of oil per ephah.
On the day of the New Moon he shall offer an unblemished young bull, six lambs, and an unblemished ram.
He shall provide a grain offering of an ephah with the bull, an ephah with the ram, and as much as he is able with the lambs, with a hin of oil per ephah.
When the prince enters, he shall go in through the portico of the gate, and he shall go out the same way.

When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by the north gate to worship shall go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate shall go out by the north gate; no one shall return through the gate by which he entered, but each shall go out by the opposite gate.
When the people enter, the prince shall enter with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.
At the festivals and appointed feasts, the grain offering shall be an ephah with the bull, an ephah with the ram, and as much as one is able with the lambs, with a hin of oil per ephah.

When the prince makes a freewill offering to the LORD, whether a burnt offering or a peace offering, the gate facing east shall be opened for him; he shall offer his burnt offering or peace offering as he does on the Sabbath day, then go out, and the gate shall be shut after he goes out.
You shall provide an unblemished year-old lamb as a daily burnt offering to the LORD; you shall offer it every morning.
Every morning you shall provide with it a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah and a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour—a grain offering to the LORD, a permanent statute forever.
So they shall provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the oil every morning as a regular burnt offering.
Thus says the Lord GOD: If the prince gives a gift from his inheritance to any of his sons, it shall belong to his descendants; it shall be their property by inheritance.

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it shall belong to that servant until the year of liberty, then it shall revert to the prince; his inheritance belongs only to his sons—it shall be theirs.

The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance by evicting them from their property; he shall provide an inheritance for his sons from his own property, so that none of My people will be driven from his property.
Then he brought me through the entrance beside the gate into the holy chambers facing north, which belonged to the priests, and behold, there was a place at the far western end.

He said to me, 'This is the place where the priests shall boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to carry them out into the outer court and transmit holiness to the people.'
Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to its four corners, and behold, in each corner of the court there was a small court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty cubits long and thirty cubits wide; all four corners had the same dimensions.
Around the inside of the four courts was a row of masonry, with cooking-hearths built at the base of the masonry all around.
He said to me, 'These are the kitchens where those who minister at the temple shall boil the sacrifices of the people.'
